item.title: Mechanical Changes
item.description: You can use strategy and roleplay to gain advantages during fights. Flanking is boring and lazy, I prefer to reward roleplay and in-game strategy. You can only Long Rest at Inns / Homes, Long Resting focusses more on mental fatigue and the ability to unwind. When you are on the road/not at an inn or home. However, you can Short Rest even in Dungeons so long as you have 1 hour spare. Long Rests for everyone (including Elves and any species that says otherwise) is 8 hours. Due to the nature of the campaign, you're characters will often not feel safe on the road and stay alert. Those "Long Rests" are where you're able to lower your guard without punishment. Heroic Inspirations more than likely will be handed out like candy, these can be used to roll any d20 (attack roll, saving throw, skill check etc) at advantage. Using it on a Disadvantage Role causes it to become a Neutral Roll (Roll-Once). Using it on an Advantage Role does nothing. These do not stack. Super Inspiration is handed down either because of DM mistakes or Player's feeling shafted by something. This turns any roll into an advantage roll. Using it on a Disadvantage Roll lets you re-roll any roll (Attack Roll, Damage Roll, Encounter Roll, etc) again at Advantage. Using it on an Advantage Roll lets you roll once more at Advantage, you must take the highest option of all four rolls though. These do stack! Dramatic Inspirations are handed once per session and do not roll over to the next session, they contain abilities ranging from the mundane ranging to the game-breaking. You are not allowed to disclose what your Dramatic is to the players until the end of the session to avoid colluding. There are rare occasions that these will stack. Heroic Inspirations are pretty standard, Super Inspirations also exist because I am not perfect and will make mistakes. Dramatic Inspirations help provide an element of controlled chaos and can let a player have the ability to completely flip the dynamics in a moments notice. Your characters aren't brain dead, they will eat and drink when they need to. Sure, while those "Feast Moments" are nice, we don't need to play Rust. Your gear and rations don't maintain themselves, after an indiscriminate amount of time you will need to cough up coin to stock up on rations and maintenance supplies for your gear. Mainly an addition to the rule of common sense, while "Shopping Sessions" are nice, spending 2 hours discussing the logistics of travel is rather tedious and can take away from the flow. Think of it as background maintenance. Tools like Thieves' Tool are rolled using the [Associated Ability Roll]+[Modifier]+[Proficiency Bonus] if proficient. The tools are assigned as such: Strength: Carpenter's Tools, Cobbler's Tools, Mason's Tools, Smith's Tools, Woodcarver's Tools Dexterity: Calligrapher's Supplies, Potter's Tools, Leatherworker's Tools, Painter's Supplies, Weaver's Tools, Thieves' Tools Constitution: Glassblower's Tools Intelligence: Tinker's Tools, Gaming Sets, Navigator's Tools Wisdom: Alchemist's Supplies, Brewer's Supplies, Cartographer's Tools, Cook's Utensils, Jeweller's Tools, Herbalism Kit, Poisoner's Kit, Land Vehicles, Water Vehicles Charisma: Disguise Kit, Forgery Kit, Musical Instruments I personally think this helps set Thieves and Artificers above others in-terms of tool usage. Formula is DC = 10 + Spell Level + (Damage Received / 4) Scales better in my personal opinion No Silver or Copper. Self Explanatory. I know what you're thinking "What the fuck is Electrum and why are we using it!?", you'll learn in time in regards to Electrum. Gold is used for largely everything in the Overworld. There is homebrew Pantheon (with familiar names, no doubt). However, knowledge of some gods is higher than others. To be decided. The choices are Double Damage Dice or Double Damage. We'll more than likely discuss it Session 1 or Session 0. Each Level of Exhaustion instead provides a cumulative -2 to all attack rolls, saving throws and ability checks. Your Spell DC is lowered by the same amount as your exhaustion levels. Your Speed is reduced by 5 X [Exhaustion Level] in feet. You die when this reaches Level 6. A Long Rest alleviated one level of exhaustion. Spending a Week Downtime in a somewhere you own or an inn you rented automatically clears all levels of exhaustion (provided you are able to get consistent long-rests through the week). I just don't like remembering all of the effects of the different levels of exhaustion honestly lol

item.title: index
item.description:
Welcome to the campaign! This index serves as your central directory for all homebrew rules, character creation guidelines, and setting-specific mechanical adjustments.Please review these pages before creating your character or during gameplay: Mechanical Changes: Core rule adjustments, including strict resting on the road, flanking alternatives, custom inspiration types, tool rescaling, and concentration formulas.
Changed Races: Lore and mechanical details for exotic races (such as 2nd Generation Warforged) in this setting.
Banned Races: A list of races that are extinct, unavailable, or considered vermin in this world (e.g., Drow, Goblinoids, Kobolds, and certain Spelljammer/Eberron options).
Changed Classes: Key modifications to core classes (Martials, Barbarians, Clerics, Warlocks, and Wizards).
Banned Classes: Classes and sources that are not permitted (such as Blood Hunter, 5.5E Content, and general homebrew).
Changed Subclasses: Balance and usability tweaks for specific subclasses (Battle Master Fighter, Thief Rogue, and Divination Wizard).
Banned Subclasses: Restricted or banned subclasses due to balance or campaign lore (e.g., Twilight/Peace Clerics, single-level Hexblade multiclass dips, and Order of Scribes).
Changed Spells: Spell adjustments for narrative and balance purposes (e.g., Revivify soul corruption, Goodberry, Sending, Identify, and Leomund's Tiny Hut).
Banned Spells: Spells that do not exist or are strictly forbidden in this setting (e.g., Silvery Barbs).

item.title: Banned Races
item.description: You'd be surprised how many people forget... They were driven extinct during the Lich King's Reign, a lot of people blamed Drow Elves for the Lich King's Rise opting to persecute them to death. They too went extinct, however less is known about the Arctic Waste dwellers. Honestly, most of the Spelljammer book is strange. Honestly, most of the Spelljammer book is strange. Honestly, most of the Spelljammer book is strange. Honestly, most of the Spelljammer book is strange. Honestly, most of the Spelljammer book is strange. This one is especially silly, they just stuffed Warlock Subclass non-sense in a Race? I need to remember that Eberon is hit or miss when I buy these books... I don't even know what the hell this even is, a diet-goblin? Goblins don't possess enough sense of self, they're considered Vermin of the Dungeons in this world. Similar to above, big rats. Bugbears lack the ability to speak common, they're closer to "D&D bears" in this world. Kobolds don't possess enough sense of self, they're considered Vermin of the Mines in this world. Fairies don't possess enough sense of self, they're considered Vermin of the Feywild in this world.

item.title: Changed Spells
item.description: After the third revive, the soul becomes more prone to corruption and can forget it's own shape causing deformations such as missing limbs, extra limbs and potentially worse. Not only is magic largely illegal in two large countries but also it prevents players from thinking "Nah, I'd resurrect" when charging into battle knowing they have a Cleric. Provides nourishment for a week instead of a day. You're travelling in weeks and this will also cut down the "Tax of Common Sense" (explained further down) Only works on objects imbued with magic, anything mechanical and without magic doesn't work and requires appraisals from an Engineer/Artificer. NO, WHY ON EARTH WOULD IDENTIFY WORK ON NON-MAGIC SHIT? Changed to not cover other planes. You can allow yourself to be used as a conduit for someone else to send their message to their target of choice, however the Conduit also hears the message both ways. Honestly, it creates narrative problems early on to sending across planes and I really can't be bothered with the 5% chance. Contact Other Plane has been bolstered to reflect this as well as the additional usage. This is not a spell you can learn through normal means and use of it in the Kingdom of Graodom without a license will grant fines due to Leomund owning this spell. This is locked behind a line of quests for Leomund, in Graodom. Due to mechanical changes surrounding how often you can get Long-Rests, a Level 3 spell would invalidate most of it. To add, this also allows an option/route to pursue legally obtaining a license and scroll for it in-game. Yes, I know. Leomund is a dick in world too, that's the idea, he privatized a spell. Exclusive to Sorcerers, Druids and Rangers. I just don't see any other class using this spell, if anything they'd more than likely use Alter Self for Aquatic Form. You can alternatively use it to speak with someone you are familiar with (similar to Sending) without the one word limitations, being granted exactly 10 minutes of talking time. This helps give a spell that has a lot of potential into something both helpful to those willing to strike bargains and those looking for lost allies. A Simulacrum cannot cast Simulacrum, a simulacrum does not have a soul or anything to draw from. No infinite bullshit for you random mage! Cures afflictions ailing the soul. Sounds weird but I'm sure it'll make sense in due time. Using it by means of a spell-slot is an exhausting process, you cannot cast Wish again for 24 hours regardless of if you have long-rested during those 24 hours. Balancing Wish is like fighting the wind lol, this is just to prevent spam for Level 20+ :KEKL:

item.title: Banned Subclasses
item.description: Twilight Domains are cool! But the main issue is that when combat DOES roll around, it becomes difficult to meaningfully challenge the party and makes calculating encounter difficulties harder without accidentally nuking someone lol It honestly just shatters balancing lol I get it, you're a Paladin or Bard and you want to be able to max your Charisma to use your sword. That's pretty much Min-Maxing and not entertaining to DM for being honest. If you're planning on putting more levels in as a multi-class then I won't stop you. This in universe is considered an almost lost art with only say 2 people who have mastered it and 3 people who are studying it. It is considered an invaluable skill and is strictly passed down. I don't care. No.

item.title: Changed Subclasses
item.description: Know your Enemy (7th level feature) allows you to alternatively spend 10 minutes observing or interacting with another creature outside combat, you can learn all of these. -# YES, YOU DONT NEED TO HARASS ME 10 TIMES! Starting when you take this Archetype, when using Thieves Tools you can instead roll using Slight of Hand instead of Dexterity. -# This probably sounds confusing unless you read below. Portent Tweak; On your turn during combat, you can use it as normal, forcing either an enemy to take a lower option or forcing you to take the higher option. Outside of combat, you can only use it to influence rolls you make. (eg, Saving Throw, Skill Checks etc) When Initiative is being rolled, you can use Portent to change your own Initiative roll or an enemy that you can see. -# This avoids other player's agency being blatantly violated and due to the VTT nature, it's not obvious when I'm rolling everything.

item.title: Changed Classes
item.description: Those who cannot cast spells (Maximum 1st level) are granted the ability to use Strength in place of Charisma for Intimidation Checks. Additionally, you are provided a Passive Intimidation calculated Strength Roll + Modifier + Proficiency. Some will feel mildly unnerved in your presence. Keeps Martial Classes relevant, especially Barbarians. While Raging, as a bonus action, you can bang on your chest (as long as you're not wearing armor) to keep your rage going. Roll a d4 for damage, on a 1 you take no damage and keep your rage going. Haha Funny buff. Starting at level 14, whenever you make roll 9 or lower on an Acrobatics or Athletics check, treat it as a 10. Barbarians get NO love. Damn. Similar to a Paladin, you can lose your way and by proxy, your connection to your God should you squander your abilities in a way that violates your God's ethos. Should you lose your Divine Light, you will change to the War Domain. ||There will be plenty of warnings before you are cut off, just like a Paladin.|| Kinda weird how Clerics aren't beholden to the same restrictions...? This is available from Level 3 onwards instead of 10. Divine Intervention can only be attempted once per week. If your deity intervenes, you can't use this feature again for 30 days (one in-game month). Otherwise, you can use it after a week. At Level 20, this defaults back to the normal rules. This probably looks worse than it is, keep in mind that you aren't long-resting as much as you're expecting. You have the option of making requests to your patron, however the extent will be dependent on your Warlock Level, your Patron and your relationship with your Patron. At the end of the day, Warlocks are just CRAPPY Clerics that follow a Powerful Entity beseeching it's Arcane Power with actual clerics following a Powerful Entity beseeching it's Divine Power. You also have the great ability to lose your abilities dependent on the grievances of your Patron towards you personally. Similar to a Cleric losing their Divine Light, you will lose your Arcane Darkness. This will result in you pivoting to either Bard or Fighter dependent on your choice. Also kinda strange that none of the Patrons can just take their powers. This way, the experience of having magic flows can act as a catalyst for dormant latent magical potential. To Learn a Spell from a Spell-Scroll alone, It requires 500GP in materials + 24 Hours for each level. Having a Professor teach you cuts this down by half. EG) A 5th Level Scroll would cost 1,250GP + 120 hours You gain more money and this helps keep the party exploring more rather than just spending a small amount of time and gold before fucking off.
